Last night I saw The Gunman which is another in a long line of "aging leading man does action hero" movies.

The Gunman stars Sean Penn and is directed Pierre Morel who has impressive action movie credits with Taken (1) and B13.

The story is corny liberal arts undergrad fantasy fiction (corporations are evil, man), and moves a bit slowly but the action is really good. I liked the "realistic" feel of the shootouts and hand-to-hand fights that were nasty, brutal, short and don't feel choreographed. It reminded me of the excellent action from the 2006 Casino Royale. This movie doesn't go overboard on the shaky-cam so you can actually follow what is happening, unlike the Bourne series.

Penn hit the gym for this one and gets to show off both his muscles and his surfing skills. He definitely came off as believable tough (yet sensitive) guy and appeared to be well trained with the firearms despite his vocal political opposition to them.

Overall I enjoyed the movie and without spoiling it the movie is worth it just for over-the-top the big-bad gets taken out at the end.

Should you watch it? Yes

Everyone can see every transaction, thus making it impossible for someone to counterfeit bitcoin.

We will never know how many Bitcoins have been lost, and how many are merely dormant. Thus while the creation occurs at a known rate, the actual practical supply is an unknown and gradually becoming less certain.

Amagami SS's storytelling style.

It's an adaptation of a dating game, which normally translates to "harem show." This is usually a problem because, in addition to annoying harem tropes, the MC doesn't actually end up with any of the girls - to appeal to all the fans, no one of them can win - and ends up mashing together the stories told in every girls' route even if it doesn't make sense (but the MC went to the festival with two different people!).

Amagami handles it, instead, by telling every girl's story separately - four or five episodes per, start to finish. It's actually handled pretty well, doesn't feel too rushed, and it avoids being a harem show altogether. It's an older (relatively, 2009) show but it's an ironic breath of fresh air.
